nodes.label: Flow
nodes.definition: A sequence of packets travelling between one source-destination pair along the same route.

nodes.label: Best-Effort Service
nodes.definition: The default service model in which every packet gets equal treatment and no host may ask for a guarantee.

nodes.label: Bottleneck Router
nodes.definition: A router on the path that cannot be routed around, so its queue is where congestion accumulates.

nodes.label: Soft State
nodes.definition: Per-flow state a router keeps for allocation decisions that is installed and removed without explicit signalling.

nodes.label: Resource Allocation
nodes.definition: The process by which network elements meet competing application demands for link bandwidth and buffer space.

nodes.label: Congestion Control
nodes.definition: The effort by hosts and routers to prevent or recover from an overloaded network.

nodes.label: Flow Control
nodes.definition: Keeping a fast sender from overrunning a slow receiver, which is a receiver problem rather than a network one.

nodes.label: Throughput
nodes.definition: The volume of data the network successfully delivers per unit of time.

nodes.label: Queuing Delay
nodes.definition: The time a packet spends waiting in router queues before it is transmitted.

nodes.label: Power
nodes.definition: The ratio of throughput to delay, used as a single measure of how effective an allocation is.

nodes.label: Congestion Collapse
nodes.definition: The state in which useful throughput falls towards zero because the network is busy carrying retransmissions.

nodes.label: Stability
nodes.definition: The property that packets keep getting through even under sustained heavy load.

nodes.label: Jain's Fairness Index
nodes.definition: A formula scoring an allocation between 0 and 1, where 1 means every flow received an equal share.

nodes.label: Router-Centric
nodes.definition: Designs in which routers decide what to forward or drop and tell hosts how much they may send.

nodes.label: Host-Centric
nodes.definition: Designs in which end hosts infer network conditions and adjust their own behaviour.

nodes.label: Reservation-Based
nodes.definition: Approaches where a host asks the network for capacity before sending and can be refused.

nodes.label: Feedback-Based
nodes.definition: Approaches where a host simply sends and then adapts its rate to the feedback it receives.

nodes.label: Explicit Feedback
nodes.definition: Congestion signalling in which a router sends the host a direct message to slow down.

nodes.label: Implicit Feedback
nodes.definition: Congestion signalling the host infers from observable network behaviour such as loss or delay.

nodes.label: Window-Based Control
nodes.definition: Limiting a sender by how many bytes it may have unacknowledged at one time.

nodes.label: Rate-Based Control
nodes.definition: Limiting a sender by bits per second rather than by outstanding bytes.

nodes.label: FIFO Queuing
nodes.definition: The discipline in which the first packet to arrive at a router is the first one transmitted.

nodes.label: Tail Drop
nodes.definition: Discarding arriving packets once the queue is full, the drop policy that pairs with FIFO.

nodes.label: Priority Queuing
nodes.definition: Several FIFO queues served strictly in priority order, the highest non-empty class first.

nodes.label: Fair Queuing
nodes.definition: Keeping one queue per flow and serving them round-robin so no single flow can monopolise the link.

nodes.label: Bit-by-Bit Round Robin
nodes.definition: The idealised model of serving one bit from each flow in turn, which makes each share independent of packet size.

nodes.label: Finish Time
nodes.definition: The simulated time at which a packet's last bit would depart, used to order transmissions under fair queuing.

nodes.label: Weighted Fair Queuing
nodes.definition: Fair queuing with a weight on each queue, so flows can be given deliberately unequal shares.

nodes.label: Congestion Window
nodes.definition: The sender's own limit on unacknowledged data, kept separately from the receiver's advertised window.

nodes.label: Effective Window
nodes.definition: What the sender may actually transmit: the smaller of the congestion and advertised windows, less the data already in flight.

nodes.label: Loss as a Congestion Signal
nodes.definition: Treating a lost segment as evidence of congestion, on the assumption that transmission errors are rare.

nodes.label: AIMD
nodes.definition: Growing the congestion window by one packet per round-trip time and halving it whenever loss is detected.

nodes.label: Sawtooth Pattern
nodes.definition: The shape the congestion window traces over time under AIMD: a slow climb, then a sudden halving.

nodes.label: Self-Clocking
nodes.definition: Letting each arriving ACK release the next segment, so the sender paces itself to the bottleneck.

nodes.label: Slow Start
nodes.definition: Doubling the congestion window each round-trip time to find the available capacity quickly at the start of a connection.

nodes.label: Congestion Threshold
nodes.definition: The window value at which the sender stops doubling and switches to additive increase.

nodes.label: Coarse-Grained Timeout
nodes.definition: TCP's retransmission timer, historically of 500 ms granularity, which can leave the connection idle.

nodes.label: Duplicate ACK
nodes.definition: A repeated acknowledgement of the same sequence number, sent when a segment arrives out of order.

nodes.label: Fast Retransmit
nodes.definition: Resending a segment after three duplicate ACKs rather than waiting for the retransmission timer.

nodes.label: Fast Recovery
nodes.definition: Continuing from a halved window after a fast retransmit instead of dropping back into slow start.

nodes.label: TCP CUBIC
nodes.definition: A variant that sets the window from a cubic function of the time since the last loss rather than from ACK arrivals.

nodes.label: DECbit
nodes.definition: Setting a single congestion bit in passing packets so the destination can report the load back to the source.

nodes.label: Random Early Detection
nodes.definition: Dropping a packet probabilistically before the queue is full, so senders are told to slow down early.

nodes.label: Average Queue Length
nodes.definition: A weighted running average of queue occupancy, so a router reacts to sustained load rather than to bursts.

nodes.label: RED Thresholds
nodes.definition: The minimum and maximum queue lengths between which RED drops probabilistically rather than never or always.

nodes.label: Drop Probability
nodes.definition: The chance RED discards an arriving packet, rising with average queue length between the two thresholds.

nodes.label: Explicit Congestion Notification
nodes.definition: Marking a packet's header instead of dropping it, so congestion is signalled without losing data.

nodes.label: Expected Rate
nodes.definition: The throughput a flow ought to be achieving, computed as the congestion window over the smallest observed round-trip time.

nodes.label: Actual Rate
nodes.definition: The throughput a flow is achieving, measured over one sampled round-trip time.

nodes.label: TCP Vegas
nodes.definition: Adjusting the window from the gap between expected and actual rate, detecting congestion from delay before loss occurs.

nodes.label: BBR
nodes.definition: Estimating the bottleneck bandwidth and minimum round-trip time directly, then pacing packets to that estimate.

nodes.label: DCTCP
nodes.definition: A datacentre variant that scales the window by the fraction of marked bytes rather than reacting to a single loss.
